turn.user_message: What about the bed after the patient leaves?
turn.context: Beyond the playbook: the discharge reference asks Bed Management to share real bed times, and each side to check the other's.

text: The discharge does not end at the door. Today the bed stays empty 75 minutes before the next patient can use it.
bullets: Housekeeping hears late, so cleaning starts late.
The bed desk learns a bed is free only when someone calls.
Nobody checks the other side’s times. So a late discharge can be written down as an early one.
chat.pointer: Switch between Today and With both linked. Pick a step to see who acts and who checks.
chat.invite: Next, we can put the order of switching on in one place.
chat.note: A discharge ends when the next patient is in the bed.
prompts: Who at the bed desk would see this?
Where do the automations stand now?

moves.prompt: Who at the bed desk would see this?

blocks.title: The hand-over to the next patient
blocks.deck: Five steps from the patient leaving to the next one arriving. With both linked, each side checks the other’s times.

legs.name: Patient leaves the ward
legs.how: The ward marks the leaving time on the phone. Tojo passes it on at once.

legs.name: Housekeeping hears
legs.with: At once, with the bed number
legs.how: Housekeeping gets an alert with the bed number and the time.

legs.name: Bed cleaned and made
legs.how: Housekeeping marks the bed clean on their phone when it is done.

legs.name: Bed shown as ready
legs.how: The bed desk sees the bed turn ready, without a phone call.

legs.name: Next patient in the bed
legs.how: The time the next patient arrives is recorded. Both sides check each other’s times.

blocks.condition: Past 30 minutes, the hand-over is slow, or a time is not what really happened. This check needs the bed desk’s own times.
